summary: Returns the value as a slug, or throws.
description: Starts with a letter, then letters, digits, hyphens and underscores — the shape a URL segment or a key can take. Spaces, leading digits and an empty string are rejected.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as a slug.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is not a slug.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireValidSlug("my-page"); // => "my-page"
requireValidSlug("a_1"); // => "a_1"
requireValidSlug("1-page"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireValidSlug("my page"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
